q1: SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, (SELECT * FROM R2 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM R3) AS Y
q2: SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, R2 AS Y UNION ALL SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, R3 AS Y
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, (SELECT * FROM R2 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM R3) AS Y
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, R2 AS Y UNION ALL SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, R3 AS Y
counterexample: INSERT INTO R1 (X) VALUES (1); INSERT INTO R2 (X) VALUES (2, 3); INSERT INTO R3 (X) VALUES (3, 4);
explanation: Q1 performs a Cartesian product between R1 and the union of R2 and R3, while Q2 first performs Cartesian products between R1 and R2, and R1 and R3, and then unions the results. This difference in the order of operations and the use of UNION ALL can lead to different results if R2 and R3 have common values.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have common values in R2 and R3 to trigger the difference in results between Q1 and Q2.
